story:
The Guardian keeps the tower stair; the Keeper keeps everything else. Master Meical of the school of making built it after the Guardian, from what the households say was the oak of the same felling, as large again as a man on a man's shoulders, and gave it the hall's stores to keep: the iron in its bars, the oak in its planks, the copper and the glass and the strange spheres the master put at the hearts of his servants, every one counted and every one in its place.

It kept them well. It keeps them still. The households say that when the colleges burned and the master did not come out of the smoke, the Keeper went on counting, and that it counts now, at the edge of the hall, alone, an inventory that has not changed since the night of the burning because nothing has been taken out of its care and nothing put in. The drakoran who came to the hall and took the master's name found that he could set the lesser servants going again with the master's books, but that the Keeper would give him nothing. Not a bar, not a sphere. What the new Meical builds, he builds from what the forged servants bring in from the dales, which is why Thulin, uncle of Achae Smith, came home as a bundle.

The other servants do not go near it. The fort's registrar thinks they have learned that the Keeper counts them too, and that a servant that wanders off is a thing missing from its stores. When it is troubled, none of them comes to its help, and it does not call; a keeper of stores keeps them alone. It stands in its place at the hall's edge, so tall that it is seen from the fort road, and it comes at anyone who walks into its sight as a storeman comes at a thief.

When it is broken it is back before the dust is down, and the households say its count starts again from the first bar, and comes out the same.
legend: The Tower Keeper is a level 55 construct, nearly as huge as the Tower Guardian, standing alone at the edge of Meical's Hall in the south of the Dales. It is aggressive from about 500 away, but its template gives it no faction, so none of the hall's constructs come when you hit it, and nothing else stands within 1,000. No spells or styles in the data: a straight melee kill for a group of fifties, the easiest of the big constructs. It respawns in about 80 seconds. Do not drag it into the hall proper, where the Guardian and its helpers are.

loremasterTopic.text: The second great servant of the hall of [meical], built to keep its stores: iron, oak, copper, glass and the spheres the old master put at his servants' hearts. It still counts them, alone at the hall's edge, an inventory unchanged since the burning, and it gives the drakoran who wears the master's name nothing, which is why the forged servants take what they find in the dales. No other servant comes near it.

bookPage: From the second book of Gracien Adamson, name registrar of Fort Gwyntell. Achae Smith asked me why the things from the hall took her uncle, and I told her what the households told me. The one who calls himself Meical has the master's books but not the master's stores, because the Keeper will not give him so much as a nail. So he sends the forged servants out into the dales to bring him what they find, and they found Thulin. She asked me whether the Keeper would have given her uncle back. I said the Keeper does not give anything back. It only counts. She said then somebody should count her uncle, and I have, in this book, with no mark beside him.
